newsitem.title: PERU: Peru awards La Oroya purchase to Doe Run Co.
newsitem.headline: Peru awards La Oroya purchase to Doe Run Co.

text.p: Peru's state miner Centromin said Friday it had given purchase rights of the La Oroya metallurgic complex to Doe Run Co following the decision by Mexico's Penoles to withdraw its offer.
Doe Run, the largest integrated lead producer in the United States and a subsidiary of Renco Group of New York, was runner-up to Penoles in an April 18 auction for rights to La Oroya.
A statement from Centromin gave no financial or other details of the deal with Doe Run.

Penoles surprised the mining world Thursday by abandoning plans to acquire a 60 percent stake in the complex "because the requirements that Penoles had set to guarantee adequate profitability did not come together."

It had previously agreed to pay the government $33.98 million and inject $192.55 million as fresh capital into a mixed company managing the asset, according to Centromin. The state miner was to keep a 40 percent stake, of which La Oroya's workers would have the right to buy a 10 percent package.
